events.title: Ink Against Borders 2025
events.description:
Sea-Watch und Ink against Borders laden zum dritten Mal zum INK AGAINST BORDERS Event – die queerfeministische und antifaschistische Soli-Tattoo-Convention für zivile Seenotrettung, gegen das tödliche europäische Grenzregime.

24. und 25. Oktober 2025 · 12–19 Uhr · Alte Münze Berlin

Auch 2025 setzen wieder rund 60 FLINTA* Tattoo-Artists ihre Kunst für Bewegungsfreiheit ein. Zwei Tage lang stechen sie in Berlin exklusive Soli-Motive. Jede Nadel ein Statement gegen das Vergessen, jede Spende ein Beitrag, der Leben retten kann.

Tickets gibt es bereits ab 12 € pro Tag oder 20 € fürs ganze Wochenende. Sicher dir dein Ticket hier.

Mit deinem Ticket decken wir die Grundkosten des Events, von Raummiete bis Technik. So stellen wir sicher, dass jede Spende aus den Tattoos direkt in die Seenotrettung fließt. Gemeinsam tragen wir die Kosten solidarisch, damit unsere Schiffe im Mittelmeer handlungsfähig bleiben.

events.title: SOLD OUT // Das Land, das ich liebe – Voices Berlin Festival
events.description:
Berliner Premiere einer Theaterinstallation nach dem dokumentarischen Buch der Journalistin Jelena Kostjutschenko



Das Land, das ich liebe ist eine Theaterinstallation, die basiert auf einem dokumentarischen Buch der Journalistin Jelena Kostjutschenko, das in vielen Ländern zum Bestseller wurde.

Ziel des Projekts ist es nicht nur, den Zustand des heutigen Russlands bloß zu beschreiben, sondern vielmehr auf erschütternde und zum Teil beschämende Fragen zu reagieren, die in letzter Zeit an Bedeutung gewonnen haben: Wie kann man eine Beziehung zu seinem Heimatland aufrechterhalten, das in das Böse abgleitet? Wie kann man Menschen zumindest ansatzweise verstehen oder akzeptieren, die gleichzeitig Opfer und Mittäter dieses Bösen sind? Wo verläuft die Grenze zwischen Rechtlosigkeit und Gleichgültigkeit? Der rote Faden, der das Stück zusammenhält, ist die persönliche Geschichte der Autorin – ihre Erfahrungen in einer Welt, die viele lieber nicht sehen möchten. Die Inszenierung untersucht, wie Realität beschrieben und wahrgenommen wird. Autobiografische Passagen des Buches – dargestellt von einer russischsprachigen Schauspielerin – und dokumentarische Reportagen über rechtlose, zum Schweigen gebrachte Menschen in Russland – interpretiert von europäischen Schauspieler:innen – verweben sich mit visuellen und klanglichen Elementen zu einer facettenreichen, vielschichtigen Erzählung. Das Stück ist ein Versuch der Übersetzung – nicht nur von Sprache zu Sprache, sondern auch von Kultur zu Kultur, von einem Kontext in den anderen. Ist es überhaupt möglich, eine komplexe soziale und politische Realität zu erklären? Können wir einander verstehen, wenn wir die Klischees und vorgefertigten Narrative hinter uns lassen? Wir glauben: ja.

___

Regisseurin: Polina Solotowizki
Dramaturgin: Polina Borodina

Bühnenbildnerin: Vanya Bowden
Darsteller*innen: Chulpan Khamatova (Videosequenzen), Evgenia Borzykh, Leon Wieferich, Antonia Leichtle, Johanna Dähler

Generale Produzentin: Svetlana Dolya
Ausführende Produzentin: Kseniia Ignatova

Koproduktion: Kunstfest Weimar 2025

Zimin Foundation, New Generation Europe Foundation

events.title: LA LETTRE – Voices Berlin Festival
events.description:
Stand-up melodrama by renowned Swiss theater director Milo Rau. A performance that explores the events that can alter the course of a life — and a manifesto for what popular theater can be today. Festival d’Avignon 2025 premiere.


Poking fun at the premise that a young artist is shaped as much by their roles as by their family history, Milo Rau explores, in this scenic etude, the events that imperceptibly alter the course of our lives: generational conflicts, political history, love, and death. Lighthearted and full of humour, seeking to create theater by creating a community, LA LETTRE is a manifesto on what popular theater can be today. From the story of Joan of Arc to Chekhov’s The Seagull, the performance unfolds on multiple levels, in a constant back-and-forth between art and life. Even the dead return to the stage, with the help of recorded voices.

 

The result is a stand-up melodrama in the form of a double helix: as the actors — Olga Mouak and Arne De Tremerie — embark on an honest, absurd, and shocking journey through their deeply personal histories of theater — from Sophocles to casting couches, from Chekhov to the #MeToo movement — there emerges a profound exploration of the soul of the performing arts, and of the art of living itself.

____


Actors: Arne De Tremerie, Olga Mouak

With the voices of Anne Alvaro, Isabelle Huppert, Jocelyne Monier, and Marijke Pinoy

Director: Milo Rau

Text: Milo Rau and team

Dramaturgy: Giacomo Bisordi

Assistant Directors: Giacomo Bisordi, Edward Fortes

Scenic Design, Sound, Lighting, Costumes, and Props:

Milo Rau and Giacomo Bisordi

Assistant, Costumes and Props: Julie Louvain

Production: Festival d’Avignon
Part of the Voices Berlin Festival

events.title: FOREVER LOST – Voices Berlin Festival
events.description:
An interdisciplinary, two-part project by Yulia Arsen that explores nostalgia, ghost futures, and collective memory through the lens of creepy post-Soviet rituals.



First part is the solo dance performance, “Do You Really Wanna Live Forever”, created by choreographer Yulia Arsen in collaboration with experimental musician Wassily Bosch, where movements echo folk dance, Soviet athletic propaganda aesthetics, and postures shaped by cheap drug use. These collide with fragmented sound — distorted pop hits, ambient noise, and personal artifacts — creating a purgatorial space where time feels frozen, as if the artists are trapped inside a memory capsule — or have become that capsule themselves. At the heart of this experience lies an inability to truly express oneself or break free. This work embodies the absurdity of existence, where repetition, irony, and sincerity merge into a melancholic, yet strangely optimistic, loop.

The second part — “Utrennik” — is a multidisciplinary collective work by nine artists, where sound takes center stage — merging with video and performance into a form of total installation. It delves into the “utrennik” — a Soviet-era children’s “morning performance”, a ritual where cheap costumes and scripted magic barely concealed a deeper emptiness. For many who grew up in post-Soviet countries, the “utrennik” became a symbol of exhausting repetition, creation without creativity, happiness without hope. Here, it reemerges as a metaphor for broken promises and futures that never arrived.

___

events.title: Games Ground 2025
events.description:
? Games Ground 2025 – Das Gaming-Festival in Berlin kehrt zurück!

Games Ground ist zurück – und dieses Jahr größer denn je! Nach einem unglaublichen Event 2024 mit über 4.500 Besuchern wird das Festival auf VIER Tage voller Gaming, Networking und Brancheneinblicke erweitert. Freuen Sie sich auf den 13. bis 16. November in der Alten Münze, Berlin.

? Business Days (Nov 13-14) bieten ein erweitertes B2B-Programm mit kuratierten Vorträgen, Panels und Workshops zu Themen wie Game Development, Publishing, Community-Building und Branchenwachstum. Mit Initiativen wie Publisher Connect, Mentor Ground und Career Ground ist Games Ground 2025 der perfekte Ort für Networking und Karrierechancen in der Gaming-Branche.

? Public Days (Nov 15-16) erreichen das nächste Level mit zwei actiongeladenen Tagen! Freuen Sie sich auf Esports-Turniere, Cosplay-Wettbewerbe, Live-Musik, Quizshows, Indie-Game-Showcases und Influencer-Content auf drei Bühnen. Außerdem erwartet Sie eine riesige Ausstellungsfläche mit Retro-Gaming, XR-Erlebnissen, Tabletop-Spielen und einer LAN-Zone.

? Alte Münze, Berlin
? 13.–16. November 2025
?️ Tickets sind ab Mai erhältlich 

Seien Sie dabei bei Games Ground 2025! ?

events.title: Cannabis Normal! Konferenz 2025
events.description:
Die fünfte Auflage der CaNoKo wird vom 21. bis 23. November in Berlin stattfinden.

Inhaltlich wollen wir an der CaNoKo 2024 anknüpfen und uns mit der Umsetzung des CanG befassen, also der Frage, wie gut bzw. schlecht das CanG in der Realität funktioniert? Zugleich wird wie schon bei der letzten CaNoKo die politische Lage erneut extrem unklar sein. Wenige Wochen nach der Bundestagswahl wird vermutlich noch keine Regierung stehen und die Frage eines „Rollbacks“ des CanG – wie von der CDU/CSU bereits wiederholt angekündigt – noch im Raum stehen.

Doch trotz dieser Unsicherheit können und wollen wir nicht weiter warten! Daher werden wir mit euch diskutieren und erarbeiten, wie man das Gesetz weiter mit Leben füllt.

Daher kann es nur heißen: Merkt euch das Datum vor, kommt nach Berlin und beteiligt euch aktiv an der CaNoKo 2025 vom 21. bis 23. November! Weitere Informationen zu den Speakern, genauen Programminhalten und dem Ticketvorverkauf findet ihr rechtzeitig auf der Webseite:

https://cannabisnormal.de

events.title: Mali: Personal Insights into the Humanitarian Crisis
events.description:
Die Fotoausstellung „Mali: Persönliche Einblicke in die humanitäre Krise“ gibt einen eindringlichen Einblick in das Leben von Menschen, die täglich mit den Folgen des anhaltenden Konflikts in Mali konfrontiert sind. Der malische Fotograf Tiécoura N’Daou reiste im September 2025 in die Regionen Gao und Mopti, um die Auswirkungen der Krise aus nächster Nähe zu dokumentieren. Seine Bilder zeigen, wie Menschen vor Ort mit Unsicherheit, Vertreibung und klimatischen Herausforderungen umgehen und wie sie trotz allem ihre Würde, Stärke und Hoffnung bewahren.

Mali befindet sich derzeit in einer der größten humanitären Krisen der Welt, die gleichzeitig nur wenig internationale Aufmerksamkeit erhält. Rund 6,4 Millionen Menschen sind aufgrund von bewaffneten Konflikten, Zwangsvertreibung und klimatischen Schocks auf humanitäre Hilfe und Schutz angewiesen. Prognosen zufolge wird sich die Situation im Jahr 2026 weiter verschärfen.

Die Ausstellung wird mit finanzieller Unterstützung der Europäischen Union und des Auswärtigen Amts organisiert von den humanitären Organisationen Aktion gegen den Hunger, International Rescue Committee, Norwegian Refugee Council, Danish Refugee Council und Ärzte der Welt.

Ausstellungszeitraum: 21. März – 23. April
Ort: Alte Münze, Am Krögel 2, 10179 Berlin (neben dem Café „The Greens“)
Öffnungszeiten: täglich 10–18 Uhr
Eintritt: frei

Foto: © Tiécoura N’Daou

___________________

The photo exhibition “Mali: Personal Insights into the Humanitarian Crisis” provides a poignant look into the lives of people who face the consequences of the ongoing conflict in Mali every day. Malian photographer Tiécoura N’Daoutraveled to the Gao and Mopti regions in September 2025 to document the impact of the crisis up close. His images show how people cope with uncertainty, displacement, and climate-related challenges, while preserving their dignity, strength, and hope despite everything.

Mali is currently experiencing one of the world’s largest humanitarian crises, which receives relatively little international attention. Around 6.4 million people rely on humanitarian assistance and protection due to armed conflict, forced displacement, and climate shocks. Forecasts indicate that the situation is expected to worsen in 2026.

The exhibition is organized with financial support from the European Union and the Federal Foreign Office, in partnership with the humanitarian organizations Action Against Hunger, International Rescue Committee, Norwegian Refugee Council, Danish Refugee Council, and Doctors of the World.

Exhibition period: March 21 – April 23
Location: Alte Münze, Am Krögel 2, 10179 Berlin (next to the café “The Greens”)
Opening hours: daily 10 a.m. – 6 p.m.
Admission: free

Photo credit: © Tiécoura N’Daou
events.excerpt: Step inside Mali’s crisis through the eyes of those who live it.

events.title: METANOIA — Art of Transformation
events.description:
METANOIA — Art of Transformation is an immersive experience where movement, fashion, sound, light and visuals converge into a shared space of becoming.
What begins as a choreographic exploration of transformation gradually evolves into a shared field where performers and audience inhabit the same rhythm of light, visuals, sound and movement. As the boundaries between performers and audience dissolve, witnessing transforms into participation.
Five dancers appear as living garments, moving from individual states into a shared constellation. The audience is free to move within the space, witnessing the transformation from different perspectives as the boundaries between performer and observer gradually dissolve. The experience then flows into a DJ set and visual environment where sound, projections and rhythm invite the audience into a collective celebration of movement and connection.

events.title: GATE TO // Hannah Uhlmann
events.description:
The installation ‚Dream of a kid‘ by @hannah_uhlmann will be on view at GATE TO space in the courtyard of Alte Münze from May 3 to May 24, 2026. It can be viewed from outside, day and night.

☆ Soft opening is on Sunday, May 3 at 3pm ☆

‚Dream of a kid’ explores childhood memories shaped by the early digital age, combining AI generated imagery, early computer aesthetics and sculptural elements.
Drawing on her own early experiences with computers and digital tools, Hannah Uhlmann reflects on the boundless logic of childhood imagination, where images are freely combined, distorted and constantly reconfigured.

Hannah Uhlmann (born 1999 in Leipzig, Germany) is currently pursuing her Master’s degree in Media Art and Design at the Bauhaus-Universität Weimar.
Mostly she is working with photography, digital media and installation, often combining different materials and approaches and sometimes including performative elements. In recent time, she has focused on 3D design and animation, while critically engaging with artificial intelligence and exploring both contemporary and traditional textile practices.
A central focus of her work lies in the interplay between digital and analog processes, translating physical realities into digital forms and bringing digital elements back into physical space.

°｡⋆⸜ ✩?✮･*✧

*GATE TO is a permanent exhibition space at the site of Alte Münze. The former doorman’s house enters into dialogue with its urban surroundings, opening the boundaries between art and public space.

events.title: GATE TO // Barbara Stepczynski
events.description:
The installation ‚The Beauty of Individuality  and the Uncomfortable Diversity’ by Barbara Thoma will be on view at GATE TO space in the courtyard of Alte Münze from July 4 to July 31, 2026. It can be viewed from outside, day and night.

☆ Opening is on Saturday, July 4th ☆

This exhibition explores the beauty and complexity of cultural diversity in our society. It views individuality as something valuable that shapes and enriches our society made visible through graffiti, artistic uniqueness, and personal forms of expression.

Each artist brings their own story, their own language, and their own unique perspectives. From this diversity emerges a vibrant tapestry of identities and their uniqueness.

The exhibition poses a central question: Must beauty be orderly, pristine, and controlled? Or does it arise precisely where differences become visible?

The beauty of diversity is not always comfortable. It challenges us; it demands our openness and willingness to question familiar notions.

Historically, graffiti has been considered uncensored and illegal nonconformist. It pushes its way from the underground to the surface and makes diversity uncomfortable in a radical way.

At the same time, graffiti breaks with the classical concept of beauty.
For many people, it is not design, not beauty, but simply vandalism. It doesn’t belong here.

The exhibition views diversity not as a contrast, but as a connection a network of perspectives that spans people, cultures, and borders.

°｡⋆⸜ ✩?✮･*✧

*GATE TO is a permanent exhibition space at the site of Alte Münze. The former doorman’s house enters into dialogue with its urban surroundings, opening the boundaries between art and public space.

events.title: Deep Fake // A Mockumentary Performance
events.description:
On May 30, the mockumentary performance “Deep Fake” will take place twice in the Prägerhalle.

“Deep Fake” combines documentary theatre with performance art and invites the audience into the controlled, almost oppressive production process of digital avatars. The stage resembles a film studio: simple props, a green screen, and reduced, cold lighting create an artificial working atmosphere. The performers follow precise instructions almost like machines. They sit motionless, speak with a controlled smile, and move in a minimalist way. This deliberately reduced physicality makes the growing alienation within the production process visible.

As the performance progresses, the boundaries between reality and fiction begin to blur. An atmosphere of increasing disorientation emerges for the audience, where proximity and distance gradually dissolve. “Deep Fake” thus explores fundamental questions of our present: How does digital technology change our perception of reality? And what happens to human connection in a system increasingly shaped by control, data, and artificial intelligence? At its core, it observes the present: despite physical proximity, it is becoming increasingly difficult for people to truly perceive one another. Communication becomes fragmented, attention dispersed, and relational experiences fragile.

The performance understands artificial intelligence not as the cause of this development, but as a mirror of existing tendencies and as an amplifier of questions that have long been embedded in society.
events.excerpt: „Deep Fake“ combines documentary theatre with performance art.

events.title: Fête de la Musique x Open House
events.description:
Join us for a special celebration of the Fête de la Musique as we open our doors for an all-day Open House filled with live music, open studios and workshops. Come by, discover the space, and celebrate music with us.

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

The Line Up

Outdoor Line Up:

Karl Kobs

Icey Planet

De Feo

Indoor Line Up:

Whisker for President

Streichelt

Wooly Aziz

Softblech

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

Karl Kobs

Karl Kobs is part of the German based duo SAL. Founded in 2014, together with his partner Max Horn they played a variety of clubs since then. Together with Joe Davies he co-runs a party at the infamous Golden Pudel Club in Hamburg since 2024, inviting Deep House affiliates such as Dana Ruh or Barbara Preisinger.

Courtyard Stage: 3pm-5pm

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

Icey Planet

Berlin-based live DJ and producer Icey Planet creates immersive electronic journeys where industrial textures, hypnotic rhythms, and organic resonance coexist. Drawing from deep house, minimal techno, and leftfield electronics, her performances unfold through fluid rhythmic shifts and evolving sonic environments, blurring the boundaries between club functionality and emotional live instrumentation.

Courtyard Stage: 5pm-7pm

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

DE FEO

DE FEO is an Italian eclectic artist and curator based in Berlin, known for blending electrifying beats and performances to create unforgettable multisensory experiences. His captivating energy has made him impose his sound on European and Asian and Mexican dance floors. His innovative approach continues with fast minimal techno and experimental music, having signed with Flash Recordings in 2021, his music research space from brought different shapes of techno, ambient and house. Notable performances in the past years includes a live A/V set in collaboration with a renomated dancer in Beijing, unforgettable DJ shows in club such as Potent Shanghai, Enter Tokyo, Kit Kat Club Berlin, R.Lounge Shibuya, Pillbox Beijing, along with a sold-out show at Alcatraz Milano in April 2024.

Courtyard Stage: 7pm – 9pm

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

Whisker for President

“Whisker for President of the Universe and Beyond” is a Berlin-based avant-garde progressive rock group. The band members Hanny (vocals, piano, guitar), Eli (vocals, guitar), Mario (saxophone), Mila (bass), and Fabian (drums) are on a mission to feed your heart and soul.

After playing in several Berlin locations, including Binuu Berlin, Neue Zukunft, B.L.O. Ateliers, Loge, and Supamolly, the band has just returned from their London debut, where they opened for Soft at The Lexington.

Prägehalle: 6pm – 6.45pm

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

Softblech

Fresh, loud, and impossible to ignore. Though the Hamburg-based band has been around for less than a year, they’ve already started making serious waves. With their debut single “Love Me Now,” they made their sound clear from the start: infectious hooks, relentless energy, and just the right amount of edge.

Prägehalle: 7pm – 7.45pm

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

Wooly Aziz

Berlin-based and Pakistan-born, Jannat Sohail creates music that refuses to sit still. Blending progressive soul, left-field electronics, and cinematic storytelling, their solo project feels both intimate and unbound by borders. Their songs drift through themes of love, displacement, war, and migration with a quiet emotional force that stays with you. Wistful vocals, immersive textures, and haunting lyricism come together in music that lingers long after the final note.

Prägehalle: 8pm – 8.45pm

✧･ﾟ:⋆｡°✩･:*｡˚

Streichelt

The Nuremberg-based indie artist crafts his own version of the Neue Neue Deutsche Welle, self-produced, razor-sharp, and emotionally unfiltered. Songs about heartbreak, self-doubt, and starting over, delivered with equal parts vulnerability and cynicism.

Prägehalle: 9pm – 1opm

Pop-up chefs Ecem from Moyo and Sophie from Soso Food will be serving a lovingly curated family-style brunch, and every guest will be welcomed with a glass of sparkling wine. Once everyone’s settled in (and perhaps already on their second glass), it’s time for bingo.

events.title: Opera Days at Alte Münze
events.description:
OPERNFEST 2026 – Berlin Opera Academy

August 25 – August 30, 2026 | Alte Münze, Berlin

The Berlin Opera Academy returns for the 11th edition of OPERNFEST, bringing nearly 300 emerging opera artists from more than 30 countries to Berlin for a month-long celebration of opera.

From August 25 to August 30, 2026, the festival presents three fully staged opera productions at Alte Münze with Humperdinck’s Hänsel und Gretel and Puccini’s Suor Angelica and Gianni Schicchi, offering audiences an intimate and immersive way to experience opera.

OPERNFEST is at the heart of the Berlin Opera Academy’s mission to connect professional training with public performance. Each summer, emerging singers, conductors, répétiteurs, collaborative pianists, directors, and orchestra musicians from around the world come together in Berlin for intensive coaching, rehearsals, and performances alongside an internationally renowned faculty.

OPERNFEST 2026 is an invitation to experience opera differently, up close, internationally, and with the next generation of performers at its centre.

Shows

  • Hänsel und Gretel by Engelbert Humperdinck on August 25, August 27 & August 29
  • Suor Angelica by Giacomo Puccini on August 26, August 28 & August 30
  • Gianni Schicchi by Giacomo Puccini on August 26, August 28 & August 30
events.excerpt: OPERNFEST returns to Berlin for its 11th edition from July 28 to August 30, 2026. Featuring nearly 300 emerging opera artists from over 30 countries, the festival presents seven fully staged productions and more than 25 performances at Theater im Delphi and Alte Münze.

events.title: VINTAGE PAPER BERLIN
events.description:
Vintage Paper Berlin – A Fair Celebrating Paper as Art

September 18–19, 2026 | Kulturquartier Alte Münze, Berlin

From September 18–19, 2026, the historic halls of Berlin’s Alte Münze will become a stage for paper in all its forms. Vintage Paper Berlin is a new, curated fair bringing together around 45 international exhibitors from the worlds of antiquarian books, photography, poster art, and contemporary paper art.

At the heart of the fair is not simply the individual book, photograph, or sheet, but paper itself — as a sensual, historical, and artistic medium for text, images, and ideas.

From Rare Books to Paper Art

The traditional antiquarian book trade forms the foundation of the fair. Exhibitors will present rare books, prints, manuscripts, ephemera, fine press editions, historical Japanese woodblock prints, and other works that reveal the rich visual and material world surrounding the book.

Photography takes a central role, with international dealers presenting vintage prints, photobooks, and historical photographs — from early scientific expeditions and travel photography to ethnographic documents and later photographic works. Together, they highlight the close relationship between photography and the physical medium of paper.

The fair also explores poster art and the history of advertising, presenting original historical posters where typography becomes image and paper becomes a carrier of messages in public space.

Contemporary artists and book makers bring the story into the present. Artist books, original prints, fine press editions, and works on paper demonstrate how artists continue to explore paper as both medium and subject. Highlights include works by Strawalde (Jürgen Böttcher), Martin Furtwängler, Anna Helm, and Tim Byers Art Books, featuring positions ranging from the classical modern to contemporary art.

Paper as an Artwork in Its Own Right

At Vintage Paper Berlin, paper is more than a support for an artwork — it can be the artwork itself. Swiss publisher Rothe Drucke, for example, draws on the historic traditions of brocade and decorated papers, reinterpreting them through contemporary artistic collaborations.

Across the fair, visitors can discover, collect, and purchase works spanning centuries of paper culture — from early printing and rare books to photography, posters, artist books, and contemporary paper works.

More than a marketplace for collectors, Vintage Paper Berlin is a place for discovery, exchange, and inspiration. Set within the industrial architecture of the Alte Münze, the fair invites artists, designers, collectors, curators, and anyone interested in art and culture to explore the enduring material and cultural significance of paper.

As organiser Michael Schrottmeyer puts it: “We are bringing paper out of the second row.” Vintage Paper Berlin places this remarkable medium centre stage — celebrating its history while exploring its continued relevance in an increasingly digital world.

Vintage Paper Berlin
September 18–19, 2026
Kulturquartier Alte Münze, Berlin

events.description:
The exhibition Rough Ground by interdisciplinary artist Nancy Görlach will be on view at GATE TO in the courtyard of Alte Münze from October 8 to October 25, 2026.

☆ Vernissage is on Thursday, October 8th ☆

☆ Open Hours: If you would like to meet Nancy, she’ll be at GATE TO on October 13th from 3 til 6pm and on October 17th from 2 til 5pm☆

For Nancy, art is not something fixed. It is something that grows, transforms, and sometimes refuses to grow at all. Moving between performance, painting, new media, and installation, she creates spaces where materials, memories, and people meet. Her colourful paintings become stages, abandoned landscapes turn into places of possibility, and everyday objects become carriers of memory. Through layers of colour, movement, and digital imagery, Nancy explores the spaces and gaps that remain after something has been left behind.

For this exhibition, Nancy works with objects and glasses from the former GDR, materials that carry personal and collective memories of another time. These objects become more than remnants of the past. They hold space for change, for new encounters, and for the possibility of something unexpected emerging. The exhibition also explores the idea of the threshold: a space between one place and another, between past and present, between being inside and remaining outside.

Rather than presenting art as something to be viewed from a distance, Nancy opens up the possibility of being present. During the exhibition, she will be there on selected days, opening the doors and inviting visitors to come inside, sit together, share a tea, or have a conversation.

Rough Ground becomes a space of waiting, transformation, and togetherness. It asks what happens when we allow things to grow in their own time, when we stay with uncertainty, and when a space once defined by separation becomes a place of connection.

→ Read more about Nancy and her work here

°｡⋆⸜ ✩✮･*✧

GATE TO is a permanent exhibition space at the site of Alte Münze. The former doorman’s house enters into dialogue with its urban surroundings, opening the boundaries between art and public space.
events.excerpt: In Rough Ground, interdisciplinary artist Nancy explores transformation, memory, and the spaces between past and present. Through painting, performance, new media, and installation, everyday objects become carriers of memory, while a former space of control transforms into a place of encounter. On view at GATE TO space from October 8 to October 25, 2026.

events.title: contemp//movement: An Art Run by Alte Münze, hosted by Claud
events.description:
​Movement creates connection.

​Join us for the very third edition of contemp//movement, a running experience where contemporary art, movement and community come together.

​Every edition is shaped by a different creative voice. Every route tells a different story.

​The artwork for the first run will be revealed soon 💫

​What to expect

​• A relaxed community run (all paces welcome)
• Hosted by Claud from foroutdoorpeople
• A unique route inspired by contemporary art
• Good people, good conversations and a shared experience

​Meet your host

​Claud is a performance marketer based in Berlin, and a climber, runner and yoga teacher who spends every weekend trying to get back outside.

​A few years ago she started foroutdoorpeople, a collective for people who work normal jobs and refuse to give up on movement. From physio and climbing coaching to nutrition and yoga, everything is built by specialists who genuinely live the outdoor life.

​This run is the first time we’re bringing that community together offline in Berlin. No pace requirements. No competitive energy. Just people who love to move.

​She’s really glad you’re here.

​Details

​🕚 Meetup: 10:45 AM
🏃 Run starts: 11:00 AM sharp
🎨 Artwork: To be announced
📍 Route: Shared before the event

​After the run

​Come for the run. Stay for the community.

​We Run Your Art.
events.excerpt: Movement creates connection. Join the first edition of contemp//movement, a relaxed community run bringing together contemporary art, movement and people in Berlin. Discover a unique art-inspired route, meet fellow runners and experience the city in motion. All paces are welcome, no competition, just good people, good conversations and a shared experience. We Run Your Art.

events.title: EDEN CINEMA – A Festival for Iris ter Schiphorst
events.description:
A festival celebrating the music and artistic vision of Iris ter Schiphorst

Always deeply connected to her audience, Iris ter Schiphorst combines political awareness with poetic force, sensual sound worlds and radical formal experimentation. After classical piano training, she left the traditional path at an early age, playing electric bass in punk, New Wave and funk bands. Through her own writing, and inspired by encounters with figures such as Dieter Schnebel and Luigi Nono, she found her way into contemporary music.

In 2026, the Zafraan Ensemble celebrates her multifaceted artistic vision with EDEN CINEMA, a festival presenting a representative cross-section of her instrumental music.

Across three concerts, a multimedia-poetic portrait accompanied by a new publication and recordings, artist talks, discussions and silent films for which Iris ter Schiphorst composed the music, the festival opens up the many different worlds of her work.

A particular highlight is the performance of HYPER-DUB, featuring Dirk von Lowtzow, frontman of the band Tocotronic, performing his text together with the ensemble.
events.excerpt: Schiphorst. In 2026, the Zafraan Ensemble presents a day-long festival bringing together concerts, film, discussion, visual art and performance. From instrumental works and multimedia installations to the silent film La Coquille et le Clergyman and the performance of HYPER-DUB with Tocotronic frontman Dirk von Lowtzow, the festival explores the poetic, political and radically experimental dimensions of ter Schiphorst’s music.
